{"body":"## Problem

Agent and Conductor workspaces have no `.venv`. Nothing creates one: `.conductor/settings.toml` has only a `[prompts]` section and no setup script. Without a venv, pyright cannot resolve third-party imports (`reflex`, etc.). This surfaced during #347, where I could check only `reportUnknownMemberType` and had to leave the rest unverified.

A full local pyright run was also killed (exit 137, probably out of memory) on an ~8 GB sandbox. So syncing the venv locally would fix import resolution but may not make full-repo pyright runs reliable.

## Proposal

Add manually dispatched RWX pipelines, `.rwx/pyright.yml` and `.rwx/pyrefly.yml`, that run pyright and pyrefly with a synced venv on the exact local git state, including uncommitted changes. Invoke it from the CLI:

```
rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait
rwx run .rwx/pyrefly.yml --wait
```

Why RWX instead of a Conductor setup script (`uv sync`):

- `rwx run` uploads a patch of local state (staged, unstaged and untracked files), so verification does not need a commit or push. See the [`rwx run` reference](https://www.rwx.com/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run).
- CI memory is not constrained like the sandbox.
- It uses the same pinned toolchain and cached `deps` task as `tests.yml` and `trunk-check.yml`, so local and CI results match.

## Investigation

- `.rwx/tests.yml`, `trunk-check.yml` and `validate-assets.yml` already define a `cli:` trigger with `init.commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}`. They already run via `rwx run <file>`.
- They all clone with `git/clone` at `init.commit-sha`. `rwx run` layers the local patch on top of that clone. I haven't verified this end to end. See the open questions below.
- They share a checksum-pinned `uv-install` task and a `deps` task. `deps` runs `uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --group dev`, filtered to `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and `.python-version` so it stays cached.
- `trunk-check.yml` already runs pyright through Trunk with `.venv`, but only as a diff-only lint (`--upstream`). It has no way to run pyright on a chosen set of files or on the whole project.
- `rwx dispatch` is a different mechanism. It launches a pre-configured workflow by key and takes `--param` and `--ref`, but no local patch. It is not suited to "verify my working tree".
- `pyrightconfig.json` extends `configs/pyrightconfig.json` (strict mode) with `venvPath: "."` and `venv: ".venv"`. The CI venv lives at `.venv`, so no config change is needed.
- `pyright` is run through Trunk (`.trunk/trunk.yaml`). Confirm whether it is also in the `dev` dependency group. If not, the pipeline needs either an added dev dependency or `uvx pyright` pinned to the Trunk version.

## Proposed design

`.rwx/pyright.yml` (and `.rwx/pyrefly.yml`, same structure):

- **Trigger:** `cli:` only, with no `github:` block. It is not a required status, so the merge queue is not affected (see the AGENTS.md note about path-filtered or non-reporting checks).
- **Tasks:** `code` (`git/clone`), `uv-install` and `deps`, copied from the existing files. Then a `pyright` task with `cache: false`, matching the other pipelines. Consider factoring out shared setup into one reusable definition, because it is now duplicated four times.
- **Targets:** an optional `init` parameter, for example `--init paths="app/foo.py app/bar.py"`, defaulting to the whole project. It lets an agent verify specific files quickly.
- **Rule filter:** optionally another `init` parameter that restricts output to one rule, for example `reportUnknownMemberType`.
- **Output:** use `--outputjson` and exit nonzero on errors, so `rwx run --wait --json` is usable by agents.

## Second pipeline: pyrefly

pyrefly is a separate checker that Trunk already runs (`pyrefly-plugin` v0.2.1 in `.trunk/trunk.yaml`). It needs its own pipeline, `.rwx/pyrefly.yml`, with the same `cli:` trigger and `code`, `uv-install` and `deps` tasks. Run it as `uv run pyrefly check`, which reads `pyrefly.toml` (`project-includes` covers `app`, `cli`, `components`, `scripts` and `tests`).

- `pyrefly.toml` sets `search-path = ["."]` and `python-interpreter-path = ".venv/bin/python"`. Both resolve relative to the config file, so they work in the RWX checkout once `deps` has created `.venv`.
- Keep pyrefly separate from pyright so each can be run, cached and failed independently, and so their results are not mixed.
- Confirm `pyrefly` is in the `dev` dependency group (it isn't visible in `pyproject.toml`). If it isn't, add it or pin `uvx pyrefly` to the version the Trunk plugin uses.
- Accept the same optional `paths` init parameter as the pyright pipeline.
- Because the two pipelines share setup, this strengthens the case for factoring the shared tasks out.

## Open questions

1. **Patch handling:** `git/clone` is given an explicit `ref`. Confirm that `rwx run` still applies the local patch in that case, and does not just check out the pushed sha. Before relying on this, test with an uncommitted edit that is known to fail pyright.
2. **Unpushed commits:** if HEAD has not been pushed, can the clone still resolve it? Document the push-first requirement if not.
3. **Scope:** should this one pipeline also run `trunk check` and `pytest` on demand, or stay pyright-only? `tests.yml` and `trunk-check.yml` already work with `rwx run` and could just be documented.
4. **Docs:** add the `rwx run` workflow to `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `.entire/agent-guide.md`. Agents should reach for it when there is no `.venv`, instead of retrying locally.
5. **Local venv:** should we also add a Conductor `[scripts] setup = "uv sync --frozen"`, or is RWX the only supported verification path? Both can coexist. The setup script helps editing and quick tests; RWX covers heavy checks.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait` and `rwx run .rwx/pyrefly.yml --wait` each checks the local working tree, including uncommitted and untracked files, and fails on a deliberately introduced pyright error.
- [ ] The pipeline can be narrowed to specific files, and the narrowing is documented.
- [ ] The pipeline is not a required status and does not run on PRs or pushes.
- [ ] The workflow is documented where agents will find it.
- [ ] The `deps` task is cached across runs when the lockfile is unchanged.

## References

- #347: pragma removal that exposed the gap
- [`rwx run`](https://www.rwx.com/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run), [init parameters](https://www.rwx.com/docs/init-parameters), [CI reference workflow](https://rwx.com/docs/rwx/guides/ci)
- `.rwx/tests.yml`, `.rwx/trunk-check.yml`, `.trunk/trunk.yaml` (pyright override), `pyrightconfig.json`

# On-demand pyright with a synced venv. Manual only: no github trigger, so it
# never runs on PRs or pushes and is not a required status.
#   rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait
#   rwx run .rwx/pyright.yml --wait --init paths="app/foo.py app/bar.py"
# `rwx run` layers the local working tree (incl. uncommitted/untracked files)
# on the clone; HEAD must be pushed so `commit-sha` resolves.
on:
  cli:
    init:
      commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}
      paths: ""

base:
  image: ubuntu:24.04
  config: rwx/base 1.2.0

tasks:
  - key: code
    call: git/clone 2.2.0
    with:
      repository: https://github.com/elviskahoro/buridan-ui.git
      ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}

  # Checksum-pinned uv installer: fails closed if the script at the versioned
  # URL ever changes. No packaged uv/install leaf exists in the RWX catalog.
  - key: uv-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      script="$(mktemp)"
      trap 'rm -f "${script}"' EXIT
      curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.11.29/install.sh -o "${script}"
      echo "504a79fd2ed0dcd47e7f04f0792cfd0871f62e24a7fe40fa8ae0f563a369f2bd  ${script}" | sha256sum -c -
      sh "${script}"
      echo "$HOME/.local/bin" >> "$RWX_ENV/PATH"

  # Filtered to the lockfile inputs so this stays cached across ordinary
  # commits. --no-install-project: sources are outside the filter; `uv run`
  # installs the project itself.
  - key: deps
    use: [uv-install, code]
    filter:
      - pyproject.toml
      - uv.lock
      - .python-version
    run: uv sync --frozen --no-install-project --group dev

  # pyright is pinned to the Trunk version (not in the dev group). Installed in
  # its own task, with no dependency on `code`, so it is cached across runs
  # regardless of source changes. The version call also fetches the node runtime pyright needs, so that is cached too.
  - key: pyright-install
    use: uv-install
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      uv tool install pyright==1.1.414
      pyright --version

  - key: pyright
    use: [code, deps, pyright-install]
    cache: false
    env:
      CHECK_PATHS: ${{ init.paths }}
    run: |
      set -euo pipefail
      # shellcheck disable=SC2086
      pyright --pythonpath .venv/bin/python --project pyrightconfig.json ${CHECK_PATHS}

Base directory for this skill: /home/vercel-sandbox/buridan-ui/.claude/skills/rwx

# RWX CLI in this repo

CI definitions live in `.rwx/` (`tests.yml`, `trunk-check.yml`, `validate-assets.yml`, `trunk-impacted-targets.yml`). Each has an `on.cli` trigger, so it can be started locally.

## Auth: two injected tokens, one per RWX workspace

Two env vars are injected into the environment, named `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_<SUFFIX>`. Each token is scoped to one RWX workspace. List the names without values:

```bash
env | grep -E '^RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_' | cut -d= -f1
```

The `<SUFFIX>` is the workspace name, uppercased. The token for this repo is the one whose suffix matches the repo owner (the owner in the `git remote` URL, e.g. `github.com/<owner>/buridan-ui`, uppercased). Use the other token only for runs in the other workspace.

The CLI reads only `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN` (or `--access-token`), so export the matching token under that name. Do this per command and never print the token:

```bash
OWNER=$(git remote get-url origin | sed -E 's#.*[:/]([^/]+)/[^/]+(\.git)?$#\1#' | tr a-z A-Z)
export RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN="REDACTED"RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_$OWNER")"
# or, one-off:
rwx runs list --access-token "$RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN"
```

A run, task, or log ID only resolves under the workspace that owns it. If a lookup returns not-found or unauthorized, switch tokens.

## Running a pipeline with your current git changes

`rwx run` sends a git patch with the run, so no commit or push is needed:

- Base: the closest ancestor of local `HEAD` that is already on `origin`. `event.git.sha` resolves to it.
- Patch on top: unpushed local commits, staged changes, unstaged changes, and untracked files.
- Excluded: anything in `.gitignore`. Git LFS changes error out; commit and push those first.
- `RWX_DISABLE_GIT_PATCH=1` turns patching off.

```bash
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --wait --fail-fast          # run CI on the working tree, wait for result
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --target <task-key> --wait  # only one task (and its dependencies)
rwx run .rwx/tests.yml --title "wip: my change" --json
```

The `git/clone` task takes `ref: ${{ init.commit-sha }}`, and the `cli` trigger sets `commit-sha: ${{ event.git.sha }}`. That wiring is what makes the patch apply, so keep it when editing `.rwx/*.yml`. Edits to the `.rwx` files themselves are also picked up locally.

## Logs and results

```bash
rwx runs list
rwx results <run-id>                          # status and failures for a run
rwx logs <task-id>                            # download logs for a task
rwx logs <run-id> --task <task-key> --output /tmp/logs
```

`rwx run` prints the run URL and ID. Use `--json` for parsing.

## Docs

`rwx docs search "<query>"` and `rwx docs pull /docs/cli-triggers` (also `/docs/cli-reference/rwx-run`).

Both pipelines work on the local working tree, including untracked files. I ran them on RWX and the results below are from those runs.

- **Auth:** the `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_ELVISKAHORO` token that the rwx skill docs tell you to use doesn't exist. The environment injects it as `RWC_ACCESS_TOKEN_ELVISKAHORO`, so I exported that value as `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN`. The injected `RWX_ACCESS_TOKEN_MARCHILI` token fails with a 403.

```bash
ls "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/design/" 2>/dev/null | grep -iE "<topic-keyword>"
```

- `*-spec-*.md` files carry motivation, constraints, trade-offs.
- `*-plan-*.md` files carry scope (and by elision, what's out of scope).
- Read the matching artifact in full before drafting.

**Git history**:

- `git log "origin/<confirmed-base>"..HEAD --format='%s%n%b%n---'` — commit subjects and bodies often capture in-flight decisions better than the final diff.

**Current conversation**:

- If the user discussed alternatives, made decisions mid-flight, or set constraints earlier in this session, those belong in Trade-offs or Risks.

If none of these sources establishes a clear Why, **stop and ask the user**. Don't fabricate motivation — a confident-sounding-but-vague Why is worse than asking.

### Step 3: Commit local changes

If the pre-flight check surfaced uncommitted changes that belong in this PR, commit them **before** running roborev — roborev reviews committed history, not the working tree, so uncommitted edits would be invisible to it.

- Stage only the files that belong in this PR. Skip tool-local cruft (e.g., `.agents/`, `.claude/`, Conductor-local files) unless the user explicitly opts in.
- Commit without asking for approval: run `git commit` directly once the files are staged. The commit message should mirror the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) — not a Conventional Commits subject.
- Do **not** push yet. Push happens in Step 11, after squash, roborev, any explicit publish request made after a preview, and the base update.

If the working tree is already clean, skip this step.

### Step 4: Squash to a coherent set of commits

**Hard gate for unpublished branches: squash before roborev, roborev before push.** A preview request stops before these steps; if the user later asks to publish, that direct request authorizes the action without separate approval of the draft. A branch is published if an open PR exists, a same-named branch exists on any configured remote, or its configured upstream points to an existing non-base branch. A local branch that only tracks the base branch (for example, `origin/<confirmed-base>`) is still unpublished. Check these in Step 1; commits on `origin/<confirmed-base>` alone do not make this branch published. On a published branch, preserve history: commit fixes as follow-ups, review that exact history, and never rewrite or force-push it.

```bash
git log "origin/<confirmed-base>"..HEAD --oneline
```

- **Default to one commit per new, unpublished PR branch.** Multi-commit PRs are only OK when each commit is independently reviewable and the slices land in order. This default does not authorize rewriting a published branch.
- Squash an unpublished branch from its merge base with `git reset --soft "$(git merge-base origin/<confirmed-base> HEAD)"` followed by `git commit`. This keeps newer base-branch commits out of the squash; Step 10 rebases onto the latest base afterward. Do not suggest an interactive rebase in non-interactive workspaces. Never use `--no-edit` flags that bypass message review.
- The squashed commit message mirrors the PR title's intent (sentence-cased, why-focused) and captures the motivation in the body. No Conventional Commits prefix.
- If the branch already has a single commit (or each existing commit is independently reviewable and ordered), skip the rebase but still confirm the count before moving on. If the branch is already published, preserve its history and use follow-up commits for review fixes; include the multi-commit history in the final handoff.
- **Never force-push to a shared branch to squash after publication.** Squash *before* the first push.

### Step 5: Run relevant tests locally, then roborev review before publishing

**Roborev reviews the diff; it does not execute the test suite.** A clean roborev pass says nothing about whether the code runs — it has caught logic/quality issues while a hardcoded assertion in a test file was still broken. Before roborev, run whatever tests cover the changed files:

- Identify affected tests by mirroring the changed path under `tests/` (many repos mirror source layout — a change to `pkg/foo.py` often has a matching `tests/.../test_foo.py`) and/or `grep -rn` the changed file's distinctive strings (a literal like an `if:` condition, a flag name) across `tests/` to catch assertions on exact values.
- Run the narrowest test target that covers the change (in a uv-based Python repo, `uv run pytest tests/<mirrored-path>`; otherwise the repo's own test command) — full-suite runs are fine too, but don't skip this step because CI will "catch it anyway": local runs take seconds, CI takes minutes.
- If a test fails, fix it now and fold the fix into the same commit (Step 3/4), *before* running roborev — don't push and let CI discover it.

**Hard gate: do not publish or move toward `git push` until Roborev reports clean, or the user explicitly accepts the reported findings or unavailable-review state after it is disclosed.** The original PR request alone does not accept findings or waive an unavailable review. This applies even if the change feels trivial, even if the diff is one line, and even if the user has not asked for review explicitly. A preview-only request stops before this review; an authorized publish request runs it before pushing.

With the squashed commit in place but the branch still local, run a local AI code review with roborev so findings surface before publication and before GitHub sees the diff. Invoke the `roborev` executable directly with the `--wait` flag; Git aliases are optional conveniences and may not exist in cloud sandboxes:

```bash
roborev review --wait
```

- `--wait` is **required**, not optional — it blocks until the review completes so findings are available before publishing. Do not run `roborev review` without `--wait`.
- A bare `roborev review` — or a leftover post-commit auto-review hook — only **enqueues a background daemon job and returns before a verdict exists**. An enqueue is not a pass: if HEAD already has a queued or running background review, block on it (`roborev review --wait`, or `roborev wait` for the already-enqueued job) so an actual verdict is in hand before publishing. Never report "review enqueued" or a missing verdict as clean.
- Capture the outcome as `clean after M fix rounds`, `findings remain (N)`, or `unavailable (reason)`. Report the same status in the final handoff. A preview-only request says tests and Roborev were not run.
- **Review loop:** follow the shared Roborev policy in General Preferences, which Conductor appends to every agent session. After each finding batch, commit fixes and re-squash an unpublished branch per Step 4 before rerunning review. If the branch is already published, keep follow-up commits, preserve their history, and squash at merge instead of rewriting or force-pushing. Ask the user as soon as a finding requires a major architecture/refactor, public-interface change, product/design decision, or scope expansion. Continue with independent findings while waiting, but do not publish while a required decision is pending. If the user declines a change, record the finding as parked or out of scope; the user may then explicitly name the remaining findings and ask to publish with them. A direct PR request by itself does not accept unresolved findings. If Roborev is unavailable, report the blocker and ask whether the user explicitly wants to proceed without review; the original PR request is not that approval. Push only after a clean review or the user's explicit current-turn acceptance of the listed findings or unavailable-review state.
- If General Preferences is absent, keep fixing actionable findings with no round or per-finding cap until resolved or blocked by a major architecture/refactor, interface/product decision, or scope boundary. Report progress after each pass; ask about blockers and continue with other findings. If Roborev is unavailable, say so and ask whether to proceed.
- For deeper fix/refine loops, consult the repo's roborev guide skill if it ships one.

### Step 6: Draft the title

The title is a formal, sentence-cased statement of **why this change exists** — not a conventional commit subject. A reviewer scanning the PR list should understand the *motivation*, not just the area of code touched.

Rules:

- **Formal, sentence case.** "Eliminate duplicated Attio retry logic across five call sites" — not "attio retry refactor".
- **Lead with the why, not the what.** Prefer the problem solved or the outcome enabled over the mechanical change. "Unblock Linear → Attio sync from rate-limit drift" beats "Add retry decorator to Attio client".
- **No Conventional Commits prefix.** Do **not** use `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `chore:`, `docs:`, etc. Even if recent commits or PRs use them, PR titles in this ecosystem are full sentences. Commit messages and PR titles are different surfaces.
- **Under 70 characters where possible**, but clarity wins over brevity — GitHub truncates in list views, so front-load the most important words.
- **Specific.** "Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts" — not "Bug fix" or "Improvements".
- **No ticket IDs in the title.** They go in Links.
- **No trailing period.**
- **Avoid bare imperative verbs** like "Add", "Fix", "Update" as the first word when a why-framing is possible. They're allowed when the why genuinely is the action (e.g., a clear bugfix), but check first whether the motivation can lead instead.

Good vs. bad title shapes:

| Bad (conventional / what-focused) | Good (formal / why-focused) |
| --- | --- |
| `feat: add retry decorator` | `Consolidate Attio retry logic to unblock Linear sync` |
| `fix: pagination bug` | `Fix off-by-one in Apollo pagination cursor causing missed contacts` |
| `refactor: clean up attio client` | `Eliminate divergent retry behavior across Attio call sites` |
| `chore: bump deps` | `Bump httpx to 0.27 to pick up the connection-pool leak fix` |

### Step 7: Draft the description

Use this template. **Drop sections that have nothing meaningful in them** — a section containing "None" or "N/A" is worse than no section.

```markdown
## Why
<1-3 paragraphs. Lead with the problem or constraint. State the motivation. Reference upstream context (ticket, spec) by link, not paraphrase. The reviewer should finish this section understanding what would happen if the PR were *not* merged.>

## Trade-offs
<Only if there were meaningful alternatives. Format: "Chose X over Y because Z." Skip if the approach was obvious or there was only one reasonable way.>

## Risks
<What could break that isn't already covered by tests. Note rollback path if non-trivial. Skip for clearly low-risk changes (docs, comments, isolated refactors with full coverage).>

## Test plan
<Reasoning, not output. "Exercised X path with Y inputs because Z is the highest-risk surface." If full unit coverage exists and the change is small/obvious, skip this section.>

## Links
- Linear: [TEAM-NNN](https://linear.app/...)
- Spec: design/backlog-...-spec-01.md
- Plan: design/backlog-...-plan-01.md
- Related PRs: #NNN
- Closes #NNN (only when Step 2 confirmed this PR fully resolves a same-repo GitHub issue)
```

Section guidance:

| Section | Required? | When to drop it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Why | Always | Never. If you can't write a specific one, the work isn't ready. |
| Trade-offs | When meaningful alternatives existed | Obvious one-way changes, fixes to clear bugs |
| Risks | When the change has non-trivial blast radius | Docs, comments, isolated refactors with coverage |
